_README: Hand-maintained roster. The pipeline cross-matches these names against CORDIS grant data on every run and writes the result to data/opportunities.json under 'roster'. Fields you edit: name, inst, group, focus, why, track, status, verified, note. Everything under 'grants' is generated — do not edit it.

_status_values.read: You have read their recent work properly
_status_values.dead: Ruled out — record why in note

_track_values.salaried: Employment-model doctorate. No scholarship needed, no nationality quota. Highest control.
_track_values.svs: Requires SVS scholarship: THE top-50 institution + offer letter + age gate. Verify THE rank.
_track_values.either: Could go either way — check funding model per position.

people.name: Enrico Di Minin
people.focus: Conservation culturomics, illegal wildlife trade, social media data
people.why: Holds BIOBANG (ERC Consolidator, EUR 2.0M, to Apr 2030). His WILDTRADE grant on illegal wildlife trade ended May 2024 — that strand lost its vehicle. You cite him three times.
people.note: Proposed RESDOC supervisor. Second route: ERC-funded posts hire outside the COFUND eligibility rules.

people.name: Ricardo A. Correia
people.why: Co-author on Ladle et al. 2016, the paper that named the field. His grant started 1 June 2026 — a team being assembled right now.
people.note: Highest time-sensitivity on this list. New grants staff up within months.

people.name: Tuomo Hiippala
people.focus: Multimodal corpora, computational text and image analysis
people.why: Your co-cited author on Di Minin 2018 and 2019. Runs the methodological engine Objectives 3 and 4 need, in the same university as Di Minin.
people.note: Natural second supervisor for the multilingual classification strand.

people.name: Tuuli Toivonen
people.focus: Spatial data science, green space accessibility
people.why: Co-author on Di Minin, Tenkanen & Toivonen 2015, which you cite. Two ERC grants, both ending during 2027.
people.note: Grants end too soon to fund a 2027 start. Useful as a lab contact, not as a funding route.

people.name: Richard Fraser
people.focus: Zoonotic anthropology, multispecies infrastructure, Belt and Road
people.why: Trade corridors, spillover risk and multispecies relations in one project — the only grant in the whole ERC record that combines your Objective 1 and Objective 2 explicitly. Starts Sep 2026, runs to Aug 2031.
people.note: Norwegian doctorates are salaried employment. Grant has not started yet, so the team is not built. This is the single most time-sensitive entry on the roster.
people.unit: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

people.name: Deborah Nadal
people.focus: Anthropology of wildlife on the move, climate-driven range shifts, citizen science
people.why: Joins anthropologists, ecologists and citizen scientists on species redistribution and human-wildlife friction. Her prior work is on human-animal relations and rabies in India — your field context is directly legible to her. Starts Oct 2026.
people.note: EUR 2.0M to Sep 2031. Citizen-science component is a direct route for your Objective 1 detection-effort argument.
people.dept: Department of Historical and Geographic Sciences

people.name: George Adamson (+ Gagné, Natarajan, Ely)
people.focus: Climate adaptation, artificial ice reservoirs, Ladakh
people.why: EUR 10.0M Synergy grant on climate adaptation in Ladakh, running Mar 2026 to Feb 2032. A six-year India-focused environmental social science programme with four PIs — the largest team on this roster.
people.note: ERC-funded posts are hired by the PIs directly and sit outside the UKRI 30% cap. Check KCL's language requirement against your bands before investing.

people.name: Marc Brightman (+ Roudavski, Bambridge, Grotti)
people.focus: Planetary anthropology, interspecies relations, political ontology
people.why: EUR 11.1M Synergy grant on human-eel relations as a lens on damaged planetary life, Sep 2026 to Aug 2032. The strongest more-than-human match in the entire ERC record.
people.note: Theoretically rich but methodologically distant from your computational work. Consider whether your quantitative skills are an asset here or a mismatch.

people.name: Derek Van Berkel
people.focus: Geospatial data science, social media mining, cultural ecosystem services
people.why: Published directly on geotagged social media for mapping where people value nature. The closest methodological match on the uploaded list to your Objective 3.
people.note: US doctorates are usually funded by departmental assistantship, so SVS may be unnecessary. December deadlines. Verify current affiliation.

people.name: Chris Sandbrook
people.focus: Digital conservation, conservation surveillance, political ecology
people.why: The leading theorist on digital conservation and its ethics. Directly relevant to your detection-effort argument and to the ethics section of your proposal.
people.note: BLOCKED on language: Cambridge requires IELTS 7.5 overall with 7.0 per element. You hold 7.0/6.5. Retake or drop.

people.name: Kate Jones
people.focus: Bioacoustics, machine learning for biodiversity, zoonotic disease ecology
people.why: One of very few people working on both biodiversity monitoring and zoonotic risk. The strongest match on the uploaded list to your Objective 2.
people.note: Her disease-ecology work is the One Health co-supervision your Objective 2 declares it needs. Subject to the UKRI 30% international cap.
people.unit: Centre for Biodiversity and Environment Research

people.name: Walter Jetz
people.focus: Biodiversity informatics, global species distribution modelling
people.why: Map of Life is infrastructure your Objective 1 would use. His work on gaps in digital biodiversity coverage is your detection-effort problem in another register.
people.note: Verify current affiliation and whether the lab takes students in your area.
people.unit: Center for Biodiversity and Global Change

people.name: Sara Beery
people.focus: Computer vision for ecology, camera traps, long-tailed distributions
people.why: Your B.Tech in Computer Science is a genuine asset here in a way it is not elsewhere on this list.
people.note: Method-heavy and image-focused rather than social. Weaker fit to your four objectives than the ranking suggests. Admission to MIT EECS is exceptionally competitive.

people.name: Neil Carter
people.focus: Coupled human and natural systems, tiger and megafauna coexistence
people.why: Works on tigers and human-wildlife coexistence. Your WII prey-base work and Ranthambhore thesis are directly legible to him in a way they are not to most on this list.
people.note: Possibly the best fit-to-existing-CV match among the US entries.

people.name: Richard Fuller
people.focus: Human-nature interaction, extinction of experience, urban biodiversity
people.why: Extinction of experience connects directly to your Objective 4 on what engagement with nature media produces.
people.note: UQ ranks far higher in QS than in THE. Since SVS uses THE, this is probably NOT scholarship-eligible. Australia funds domestic and international PhDs via stipend scholarships, so check that route instead.
people.unit: Centre for Biodiversity and Conservation Science

people.name: Daniel Fink
people.focus: Citizen science at scale, machine learning, migration modelling
people.why: eBird is the largest citizen-science conservation dataset in existence and the strongest example of the detection-effort problem you are working on.
people.note: The uploaded list also names Steve Kelling — verify whether he is still active at Cornell before writing to him.

people.name: Carlo Ratti
people.focus: Urban sensing, mobile phone and social media data for human activity
people.why: Pioneered social media signal analysis for mapping human activity in green space.
people.note: Urban studies rather than conservation. Weakest thematic fit on this list despite the institutional prestige.

people.name: William Sutherland
people.focus: Evidence-based conservation, horizon scanning, literature synthesis
people.why: Evidence synthesis and horizon scanning overlap with your interest in what conservation evidence exists and where it is missing.
people.note: Same Cambridge IELTS block. Also senior enough that cold contact rarely lands.
